_comment: cherrypick-flies: 0DTE net-credit butterflies. Paper-only. Copy to config.json and edit. The paper DB lives under the shared cherrypick home (~/.cherrypick/data/flies/paper_trades.db); override with FLIES_DB_PATH.
_source_note: The suite's canonical shared stream cache. This module reads it READ-ONLY and runs no streamer of its own — the suite runs one streamer, not three. Omit to accept ~/.cherrypick/data/marketdata/stream_cache.db. Precondition: some producer must be streaming it — MEIC's streamer when MEIC is installed, otherwise the standalone packages/streamer daemon — subscribed to the symbols below, since open interest (and therefore GEX) exists only because the producer subscribes DXLink Summary.
_intraday_agent_note: Off by default. A model reads the session (cherrypick.flies.intraday_pack) and decides the trend gate and stranded-vertical closes for the intraday-agent paper arm; scripts/flies_intraday_agent.py makes the call, fenced like the advisor, and everything else is deterministic (intraday_advice.py). paper: whether the paper arm acts (needs no daily yes). live_mode_max: the most /live-flies-start may offer on live -- off | shadow | gates | gates_and_closures -- and a mode is offered only when this AND the qualification file allow it; the day's choice is written on that day's arm record. model is a CLI alias. trigger_band_points: call only within this of the 20-point trend line, or while a vertical is open. decision_ttl_minutes: how long a decision stands before the arm falls back to the rule. max_calls_per_session and min_minutes_between_calls bound the spend (about $0.17 a call on Opus).
_live_note: THE LIVE LOOP (docs/live-trading-plan.md). 'enabled' must be true AND 'gate0_confirmed' must carry a human attestation; the loop additionally requires a designated account (cherrypick account --module flies), refuses while the suite halt flag (state/halt-live.flag) exists, and halts new entries when the day's settled LIVE net reaches -daily_loss_halt_dollars (null = off, the deployed posture since 2026-09-17: it reads SETTLED net, so it could only ever halt the session after a bad day, and the buying-power cap below is the sizing gate instead). no_entry_before (10:15 since 2026-09-29, live-only, null = the arm's own) is the live start of day: it overlays the arm's post-open floor and can only move it later -- paper control is unbounded so its 10:00 entry costs nothing beyond itself, while live is sized by the margin cap, and the era's weakest slot (10:00-10:14) crowds that cap during the 10:15-10:30 entries that make the money. It was 10:30 from 2026-09-17 under the one-incomplete rule; with that rule gone, scripts/flies_live_start_replay.py replayed control's 25 era sessions under the cap: 10:15 +$4,758, 10:00 +$3,614, 10:30 +$2,735, and 10:15 beat 10:30 on 19 of 21 differing days (sign p 0.0002). In-sample; journaled as a live entry_rules break and watched over ten live sessions with --validate. max_open_margin_dollars (null = off) is the LOCAL buying-power cap: the worst-case exposure of every open live position plus the proposed spread's (width - credit) x 100 must fit under it or the entry is refused as max_open_margin_reached -- ledger and plan only, never a balance call, so it cannot fail closed on a transient broker error the way account_deploy_limit_pct can; one open 5-wide SPX vertical counts ~$255-300 against it (width less credit, x100; fees and the assignment reserve once open), so 1000 admits three at once. Since 2026-09-25 it is the ONLY sizing gate (see CONCURRENCY). Exactly ONE arm goes live (control since 2026-09-17: ATM centring, 5-wide, its own 10:00-14:30 window -- gex was retired from the paper roster at the 08-21 cutover and every centring alternative measured flat to negative against control). ARMING IS PER-DAY: /live-flies-start (a fresh YES every time) runs `live_loop.py --install-task`, registering a 1-min self-healing tick that SELF-DISARMS at disarm_time (and any tick finding a previous day's arm stamp disarms immediately) -- today's authorization can never carry into tomorrow; the orchestrator watchdog backstops by setting the halt flag if the task somehow survives. STREAMER BEFORE API (suite rule): all pricing reads the shared stream cache; cached quotes gate broker calls -- a resting entry order is only cancelled/replaced when the cached evaluation moved (center, or credit by >= one tick), and the burst fill-watcher (spawned per tick while orders are pending; polls every fill_watch_poll_seconds for fill_watch_seconds) only hits the broker's status endpoint when cached quotes touch the working limit or fill_heartbeat_seconds elapsed. ORDER ALERT STREAM (added 2026-07-31, use_order_alert_stream, default false): when on, the burst watcher ALSO blocks each cycle (up to fill_watch_poll_seconds) on tastytrade's own account-alert websocket for a PUSH notification of a fill/cancel/reject on any pending order -- a completely separate stream from the shared market-data cache above (this one carries order/balance/position pushes for the designated account, not quotes), used exclusively to learn about a fill sooner, never to decide anything. A push hit is treated exactly like a cache touch: still confirmed through the ordinary status-endpoint call, never a second write path. Fails closed on any websocket/auth error (falls straight back to the cache-gated poll above, byte-for-byte), so this is purely a latency optimization, never a dependency -- the poll-based fallback (and run_once's own once-a-minute re-poll) is what actually guarantees a fill is eventually confirmed. Left off by default until proven on real live sessions; flip on only after a manual read-only listen test against the real account. ORDER ALERT DAEMON (added 2026-07-31, use_order_alert_daemon, default false, supersedes use_order_alert_stream when both are on): instead of the watcher opening its own websocket per cycle, a small separate process (src/alert_daemon.py, started by /live-flies-start on arm and stopped on disarm, self-exiting at disarm_time) holds ONE account-alert connection open for the trading day and appends every alert to a dedicated WAL-mode inbox (data/flies/live_alerts.db). The watcher then reads that inbox -- a local query, no network, no handshake per cycle -- and treats a fresh row exactly like a cache touch. Deliberately a separate database from live_trades.db: the ledger's concurrency was tuned for exactly two short-burst writers (the tick and the watcher, each file-locked), and a third persistent writer would stack onto that; the inbox is the 1-writer/N-reader shape WAL exists for, so the ledger's writers are untouched. Same fail-closed posture as everything else here -- an unreadable/absent inbox, a dead daemon, or one that was never started just leaves the watcher on its ordinary cache-gated polling, and run_once's once-a-minute re-poll still confirms every fill regardless. The daemon never decides anything, never places or cancels an order, and never writes the ledger. FRESH-QUOTE CHECK (live-only, entry-only -- the one narrow exception to 'cached quotes gate broker calls', added 2026-07-30 after a live entry was rejected by the broker's real-time execution-quality check on a cached price its own preflight dry-run never flagged): immediately before submitting the opening credit-spread order, both legs' prices are re-fetched once via a plain REST market-data call (not the streamer) and the credit recomputed the same way the cached evaluation does; if either leg's fresh quote is unavailable the entry is skipped this tick (retried next tick), and if the fresh credit is worse than the cached one by more than fresh_quote_tolerance_dollars the entry is also skipped -- otherwise the order is submitted at the fresh (tick-floored) price, never the cached one. This fires only at the instant a live entry order is already about to be submitted, never on the per-tick decision path, and never in paper. COMPLETION: placed once, immediately after the entry fill confirms, resting at min(credit - fee_buffer, the min_floor_dollars-implied bound) so it can never fill at a price either gate would refuse; cancelled at completion_cutoff. SETTLEMENT: auto at settle_time from the last streamed trade marked 'last_trade_provisional'; confirm with `live_loop.py --settle --price <official print>` (marked 'official'). CONCURRENCY: max_incomplete_spreads (null = no count limit, the deployed posture since 2026-09-25) caps how many incomplete positions may be open at once -- an open short vertical always counts; a completed fly counts only if its floor is negative (not risk-free) after fees; negative_floor_override names one exact position_id to waive. With it off, max_open_margin_dollars is the sizing gate, and it counts both at their worst case. Set 1 to restore the pilot's original one-incomplete-at-a-time rule (07-30..09-25). gate0_confirmed is a human attestation, not a code-enforced statistical check -- Gate 0's sample-size bar can be knowingly waived for a small pilot; if so, say so in the attestation string. max_structures_per_day (null = off) caps ESTABLISHED structures per day -- unlike max_incomplete_spreads, a risk-free completion does NOT re-open this budget; set 1 for the plan doc's strict rung-1 one-structure-per-day posture.
_symbols_note: Traded symbol. SPX as of 2026-08-01 (XSP 2026-07-29..07-31, SPX through 07-28; every era's books remain in the ledger under their own symbol and widths, and analytics takes a `symbol` filter throughout so the eras never blend). The switch is a fee decision: on the 1-wide XSP book the median completed fly collected $12.00 against $4.97 of fees -- 41.4% drag -- while the 5-wide SPX book collected $63.12 against $6.89, or 10.9%. Credit scales with the structure; the $5-per-ITM-strike assignment fee does not. SPX and XSP are the only symbols this module should ever run -- both European cash-settled, so a short middle strike left open into expiration settles to cash and assignment is structurally impossible; a physically-settled symbol would need the assignment machinery MEIC carries.
_stream_window: The ATM-window width this module asks the streamer for, in strikes per side. base_width is the floor; stream_window.py escalates above it after repeated window-miss refusals (missing_leg_quotes, and since 2026-09-19 no_delta_quotes_beyond_spot) and decays back. request_base_width true sends the floor itself as a window hint, so the streamer subscribes it (it takes max(its own default, hint)); false keeps the older behaviour where only an escalated width is sent and the streamer's global default (30 a side since 2026-08-24, +/-150 SPX points) applies at rest. 45 a side is +/-225 SPX points: the 15-delta centre the delta arms place is ~40 points out at 10:30 on a quiet day and ~100 on a VIX-20 one, the 5-delta hedge candidate ~150 on that same morning, and the wide bwb far wing adds ~20. Cost: (2x45+1) x 2 rights x 4 events = 728 subscriptions per SPX window against 488 at the default, two windows.

defaults._wing_width: Points per wing -- the width of the control/gex/time_window books. Scale with the symbol, and note the floor is set by the underlying's own strike spacing: SPX 0DTE strikes are 5 points apart (measured: 302 of 479 gaps), so 5 is the TIGHTEST structure SPX offers and the minimum per-contract risk is $500. XSP's 1-point strikes allowed 1 ($100). Moving to SPX on 2026-08-01 therefore raised per-contract risk 5x -- unavoidable, and accepted deliberately for the fee economics in _symbols_note. Credit scaled with it (12.6% of width on SPX vs 12.0% on XSP), so it is close to the same trade 5x larger rather than a different one. The width-N sweep arms (below, in 'arms') set 'wing_width_strikes' instead of this key -- N strike increments, resolved to points against strike_increment by engine.merged_params -- specifically so their meaning survives a symbol whose strikes are not 5 points apart; this key is a raw point value and only ever applies to the arm it is set on.
defaults._max_positions: Structures per (arm x symbol) book per session. Raised 4 -> 99 (effectively uncapped) 2026-07-29 for the paper width study: in paper the fee stack is modeled, not spent, so the cap's cost/risk rationale doesn't bind and it only throttled sample accrual — every structure is an independent sample, the MEIC width-study posture. Two things still bound entries: the one-structure-per-centre rule and each arm's entry windows. Keep this EQUAL across compared arms or net-P&L comparisons measure opportunity count, not the variable under test (this module's own history records that failure twice); time_window's per-window cap of 2 stays — window-spreading is that arm's machinery, so read it per-trade against control, not on net. Restore a real cap (and rethink it per symbol) before anything goes live.
defaults._min_seconds_between_entries: Minimum seconds between this arm's ENTRY FILLS. 360 (six minutes) as of 2026-08-11, when each arm became its own portfolio with unbounded capital and buying power -- so cadence and the entry rules are the only things pacing an arm, and this is the one that decides how many samples a session can hold. The clock runs from the last FILL, not the last attempt: an order that was placed and never filled did not use the slot, and charging it for one would make a quiet market read as a throttled arm. Set on the ARM if arms are to be paced differently, but keep it EQUAL across arms being compared on net P&L -- an unequal cadence makes the comparison measure opportunity count rather than the variable under test, the failure this module's history already records twice for max_positions. 0 disables the gate. Every refused attempt records the seconds it still had to wait (fly_entry_attempts.seconds_until_cadence_clear), which is the measured cost of this number and the only honest input to changing it. CHANGING THIS IS A MEASUREMENT BREAK: entry pacing decides how many structures a session accumulates and therefore what a per-session net means, so sessions either side of a change are not poolable -- journal it the way _note_cadence_change journals a tick-cadence change.
defaults._no_entry_before: Hard post-open blackout (ET). No arm may enter before this, regardless of its own entry_windows — the gate is checked before the window logic, so an arm asking for an earlier window is refused rather than obeyed. Set to 10:00 on 2026-07-27: on the first five sessions every dollar of loss sat in the first 30 minutes (23 positions entered 09:30-10:00 ET for -$1,948.32, against +$913.79 across the 32 entered later), concentrated in control and gex, both of which opened at 09:45. Expressed as a floor rather than by editing each arm's first window because four separate window lists are four chances to silently reopen the hole when an arm is added — MEIC is the worked example of that failure mode. The arm windows below were raised to match anyway, so the two agree; the floor is the backstop, not the primary statement.
defaults._max_positions_per_window: Structures any ONE entry window may take, on top of max_positions. null disables it (single-window arms need nothing here). A global cap alone does not make a multi-window arm test its windows: over 07-20..07-24 the time_window arm put 15 of its 16 legged entries in 10:30-11:00, 1 in 12:30-13:00 and 0 in 14:00-14:30 — the book was full before the later windows opened, so the timing hypothesis was never exercised and the per-window ranking the arm exists to produce had nothing to rank. Set it on the ARM, not here, and keep cap x windows >= max_positions or the book can never fill.
defaults._entry_modes: legged = sell a credit spread, then buy the completing spread cheaper to end up holding a fly for a net credit. outright = buy a cheap fly with premium already taken in. Both were observed running side by side in the same real session, but outright is OFF as of 07-27 for two independent reasons. (1) It lost on every one of its four settled positions (-$171.31, avg -$42.83): it manufactures no floor, it spends one, so it only pays when the fly finishes in its wings, and 19 of 23 completed flies did not. (2) It was confounding the experiment — the gex arm was the only arm taking outright entries (5 of its 15), so gex vs control was no longer isolating the centring rule the way the arms are supposed to differ. Re-enable only as its own arm, never inside an existing one.
defaults._completion_modes: How an open legged credit spread may be completed. 'debit' = buy the completing same-type debit spread (the original mechanism). 'iron' = sell the OPPOSITE-type credit spread instead, producing an iron butterfly -- payoff-equivalent to a fly shifted down by wing_width, so risk-free iff the two credits summed clear wing_width plus fees (NOT assumed; the same floor gate enforces it). When both are enabled and both clear their gates on the same iteration, the higher post-fee floor wins. Off by default (['debit'] only) -- enable ['debit','iron'] only on its own arm, per the entry_modes rule above.
defaults._min_credit_pct_of_width: Opening credit floor as a fraction of wing width. Below this there is no room for the completing debit to come in cheaper AND clear two fee stacks.
defaults._max_intrinsic_pct_of_width: Refuse a legged entry whose short strike is already this deep in the money, as a fraction of wing width. null (default) disables it; 1.0 means 'refuse when BOTH legs are ITM', i.e. the spread's expiry value is already pinned at maximum loss and only a reversal through the entire width recovers it. Set on the ARM, not here -- it is opt-in and currently carried by `gex-intrinsic` alone. THIS IS WHAT max_credit_pct_of_width IS NAMED FOR AND CANNOT DO: that gate reads the CREDIT as a proxy for moneyness, and at 0DTE the proxy fails, because with hours left a fully-ITM 5-wide prices near 2.5-3.0 rather than near 5.00 -- there is still real probability of moving back out. Measured over the SPX era, all 16 fully-ITM legged entries priced at 48-59.7% of width, every one UNDER the 0.60 ceiling, so the ceiling had never once caught the case it is named for. Intrinsic is computed directly from the short strike and spot (engine.intrinsic_at_entry), so it is exact and needs no per-symbol calibration. LEGGED ONLY: bwb and debit_first carry different geometry and their own populations are unmeasured.
defaults._max_credit_pct_of_width: Opening credit CEILING. A vertical cannot be worth more than its width, so a credit near that width means the short leg is deep ITM and the premium is mostly intrinsic — a low-probability directional bet rather than a pin bet. Observed against real SPX quotes: a centre 67 points from spot produced a 77%-of-width credit with 67 points of intrinsic. The floor above cannot catch that, because a fatter intrinsic-heavy credit looks better to a floor.
defaults._min_debit_pct_of_width: debit_first's mirror of min_credit_pct_of_width: below this the debit vertical bought first is too far OTM to be plausible — little room left to richen before the completing credit spread's own width ceiling caps it.
defaults._max_debit_pct_of_width: debit_first's mirror of max_credit_pct_of_width: a debit approaching the width means the long leg bought first is already deep ITM, leaving little room for the completing sale to out-earn it.
defaults._hedge_delta: THE HEDGE OVERLAY (2026-09-19), telemetry only, legged entries, paper book. At every legged entry the ~hedge_delta option on the spread's LOSING side (a put below the long wing for a put spread, a call above for a call spread; nearest |delta| to this value within hedge_delta_tolerance, strictly beyond the wing) is priced and stamped on the row -- strike, delta, buy premium, single-leg fee -- and NEVER bought. Each tick the running MAX of what selling it would fetch is kept; at settlement its intrinsic at the same print is recorded. `python run.py hedge-overlay` then reprices every settled spread with and without it, split stranded/completed, plus a sell-at-Nx replay over the running max (an upper bound: best-ever, not a fill). The question it answers: does a far-OTM long on the losing side cut the stranded branch's loss, or does it only add premium to every entry? The spread's own decision and price are untouched. null disables the overlay; a chain with no fresh delta records nothing (hedge_strike NULL) rather than a guess.
defaults._fee_buffer: Price points the completing debit must beat the original credit by. This is the gate that stops us 'completing' into a fly whose credit is real but smaller than the fees paid to build it.
defaults._completion_price: What a legged completion PAYS once its trigger fires (the trigger -- modelled debit at or under credit - fee_buffer and the min_floor_dollars bound -- is unchanged). 'limit' (the default from completion_price_from) pays the live resting limit, engine.completion_limit = max_safe_completion_debit floored to the tick, exactly what live_orders.resting_completion_spec submits; 'modelled' pays the modelled debit (mid + slippage_frac of each leg's spread), the rule before 2026-10-05. Live fills at its limit every time (42 of 42, 2026-08-03..10-02), while paper's modelled debit had usually run past it by its tick: about $4 a completion better than live ever got. completion_price_from is the session the rule binds from, a book-wide measurement break (paper_loop._note_completion_rule); never pool completion P&L across it. docs/fill-model.md.
defaults._min_floor_dollars: Reject a completion whose post-fee floor lands below this. Was 50.0 on the reasoning that a $5-27 guaranteed profit was 'not worth the position slot or the defined risk carried while waiting'. The first five sessions falsified the premise: refusing does NOT free the slot, it leaves the position as an uncompleted short vertical, and that branch realised an average of -$208.51 per position (17 of them, -$3,544 total) against +$110.47 for a completed fly. Turning down a guaranteed +$9.36 to keep a lottery ticket averaging -$208 is the losing side of that trade. Measured over 07-20..07-24, five completions were blocked by this gate alone at floors of $9.36-$39.36; converting them moves completion rate 57.5% -> 70%, past the ~65% break-even implied by those two averages. Scaled 10.0 -> 1.0 at the 2026-07-29 XSP move (premiums run ~1/10 of SPX; the same proportional bar). DERIVED, not scaled, on 2026-08-07: -10.0. The 1.0 was inert -- ZERO of 64 completions in the 08-01.. SPX era had a floor below it, so on the completion side the gate refused nothing it saw, and live_orders.max_safe_completion_debit's resting price was set by fee_buffer alone. It was also not restorable: 576b889 (2026-08-01, 'remove the pre-close ITM exit, reserve the assignment fee instead') redefined position_floor to reserve the worst-case assignment fee ON THE SAME DATE the symbol went back to SPX, so the quantity this gates on changed too and the old 10.0 no longer means what it meant (it would now refuse 42 of 64 completions, est -$10,457). The bar is therefore derived against the CURRENT floor definition and against the measured alternative, per CLAUDE.md rule 6: refusing does not free the slot, it leaves a short vertical realising -$195.05 on average (-$170.40 in control, -$240.06 in gex). A guaranteed small negative worst case is the better of two positions we already hold; BUT the range this gate can even reach is narrow, and that is the fact that actually sets the value: the PRICE gate caps the completing debit at credit - fee_buffer, so the worst floor a completion can carry while still passing it is fee_buffer*100 - fees - reserve = 10.00 - 6.89 - 15.00 = -$11.89 on 5-wide SPX -- independent of the credit. Anything at or below -11.89 is inert because the price gate refuses first, which is the same mistake 1.0 made from the other side. So the useful band is (-11.89, +inf), fee_buffer is what really bounds the downside, and -10.0 admits nearly everything the price gate permits while staying non-vacuous. Measured: the 7 completions this gate refused over 08-01..08-06 had would-be floors of -$2.50..+$7.50 and realised -$1,287.58, four of them in CONTROL -- the one arm clearing its own break-even (analytics.break_even) -- where admitting them is worth ~+$488 against its +$409. Rule 6's second limit applies: this is an argument from a MEASURED alternative, not standing permission. Re-derive per symbol whenever the stranded branch stops dominating, and re-derive again if position_floor changes. Note this value is SHARED with the bwb roll gate (engine.evaluate_roll) -- same reasoning holds there, the un-rolled alternative carries a real tail -- and it is symbol-scaled while stored as a bare scalar, so a `symbols` change is a change to this value too.
defaults._max_fly_debit: Outright flies are bought deliberately cheap ($10-50 observed in the reference books). Points, not dollars: 0.50 x 100 = $50.
defaults._fund_from_open_credit: Whether an OPEN credit spread's premium may fund an outright fly. True matches the observed behavior (a live iron condor funded three flies), but that premium is not yet earned — which is why the book roll-up reports `unbounded_below` rather than calling such a book risk-free.
defaults._max_center_distance_pct: How far from spot the gex arm may centre a fly, as a fraction of spot. Tight on purpose: this is a 0DTE pin bet, and a centre far from spot needs a large move in the remaining hours just to reach the peak. 0.003 is about +/-22 points on a ~7500 index, roughly four strikes. Watch arm_divergence — if the gex arm agrees with control nearly always, this is the first value to revisit, because the arms can only be compared to the extent they disagree.
defaults._slippage_frac: Fraction of each leg's bid-ask conceded from mid, per fill. Matches cherrypick.core.fees and MEIC's paper engine — one fill model across the suite.
defaults._max_quote_age_seconds: Legs quoted longer ago than this are dropped as stale, and a structure missing a leg is simply not offered. On 0DTE a few minutes is a different market, and pricing a fill off an old quote produces a paper result that looks real and isn't.
defaults._max_gex_input_age_seconds: The same staleness discipline as max_quote_age_seconds, applied to the GEX surface's own inputs (gamma from Greeks events, open interest from Summary events). Much longer than the quote limit because these move on a different clock -- OI is a once-a-day exchange snapshot and gamma updates far less often than a quote -- so 120s would reject a perfectly good surface. Until 2026-08-01 there was no limit at all: an hours-stale gamma produced a GEX number indistinguishable from a live one, on the path that picks the live butterfly's centre strike (select_center, and the live default arm is 'gex'). Measured against a dead feed, the whole surface is now correctly refused.
defaults._regime_labels_note: Two thresholds that shape the REGIME LABEL stamped on every decision (up_from_open / flat / centre-offset bucket), not entry permission -- nothing is refused by them. Readable by the engine but documented nowhere outside engine.py until an audit on 2026-08-06, so they could only be discovered by reading Python. Values here are the shipped defaults; copying this file changes nothing. regime_trend_points (20.0) is the flat band: a day whose drift from the open stays inside it has not committed to a direction. It was 5 -- one SPX strike -- which docs/centre-lag.md records as reaching for a familiar number rather than a measured one. regime_center_offset_points buckets how far a chosen centre sat from spot, and is deliberately NOT listed as a key here: absence is meaningful, because it falls back to strike_increment (one strike, the resolution the centre is actually chosen at). Writing it as null would not mean 'default' -- params.get returns the null and the comparison against it raises. Set it only to a real number, and only to override the per-symbol strike increment.
defaults._min_gex_strikes: Below this many contributing strikes the GEX surface is refused rather than reported. A handful of surviving strikes still yields a call_wall and a gamma_flip that look exactly as confident as a full surface's; a real SPX/XSP 0DTE chain carries 109-121. On refusal the gex arm degrades to ATM (center_reason 'atm_gex_unavailable') rather than skipping the session -- a lost signal, not a lost sample.
defaults._book_scan_step: Price step for the book-floor payoff scan. Keep it a fraction of strike_increment (0.2x, matching the SPX-era 1.0 against a 5-point grid) or the scan only samples the strikes themselves and a trough between them goes unmeasured.
defaults._regime_tagging: engine.classify_regime tags every entry and completion (not every tick) along four dimensions, purely descriptive -- nothing here gates a decision, it exists to give a future regime-conditioned mode selector real labelled outcomes to be built from instead of guessed at. Every threshold below is a placeholder pending recalibration once real sessions accumulate, same as every other gate in this module.
defaults._regime_gex_window_pct: GEX concentration is measured only within this fraction of spot -- the region where pinning could actually act. Before 2026-08-01 it was measured over the ENTIRE chain (flies computes GEX across the whole surface, 109-121 strikes on a real session), which made 'pinning' unreachable in practice: entry_gex_bucket came back 'thin' 60 times out of 60 while the sibling vol and skew tags varied normally. Gamma 300 points away has no bearing on whether price pins here.
defaults._regime_gex_pinning_concentration: Share of near-spot gamma held by the top 3 strikes, above which the regime is tagged 'pinning'. Top-3 rather than the single largest because pinning is a property of a cluster -- a doubled centre plus its neighbours -- and a single-strike measure splits that cluster's own mass and reads it as thin. CALIBRATED 2026-08-21 from the recorded shares (605 settled SPX entries, 15 sessions): the old 0.60 guess sat above the p95 of everything ever recorded, so 'thin' swallowed 97% of rows; the cuts are now the distribution's own terciles, rounded (p67=0.412 -> 0.42, with regime_gex_clustered_concentration at p33 -> 0.30), giving diffuse/clustered/pinning with completion falling monotonically 68/63/55% -- the mechanism (near-spot gamma suppresses the drift a legged fly needs), not a boundary flattering itself. Historical rows re-bucket at read time via analytics.by_regime bucket_edges.
defaults._regime_gex_clustered_concentration: Lower cut of the three-way GEX tag: shares below it are 'diffuse', between the two cuts 'clustered'. Calibrated with the pinning cut above, 2026-08-21.
defaults._regime_time_edges: Boundaries of the open/midday/close tag. Were 10:00/15:30 and produced 'midday' on 60/60, then 97/97, rows -- degenerate BY CONSTRUCTION, since entries only ever occur inside them (measured range 10:00-14:42, median 11:19). Re-cut to 11:00/13:00 on 2026-08-06 against the recorded minute, which is exactly what that float is stored for; no session was re-run. The three buckets then split 43/35/19 with completion falling monotonically 72% -> 63% -> 58% through the day -- mechanically plausible rather than merely non-degenerate, since a legged entry completes only after spot drifts off the centre and a later entry has less session left to drift in. CHOSEN ON THE SAME 97 ROWS THAT MEASURE IT: a current best estimate, not a calibrated constant, the same standing as the trend band's 20 points. The dimension is NOT redundant with entry_window, which was the live alternative -- entry_window's dominant '10:00-14:30' window holds 74 of the 97 rows and splits 35/27/12 across these buckets, so it cannot see this variation at all.
defaults._bwb_far_width_ratio: bwb_roll's wide/risk-carrying wing, as a RATIO of wing_width (far_width = wing_width * ratio) -- not an absolute point value, since wing_width itself is manually rescaled per symbol and per width-sweep arm (control=1, width-2..width-5), and a fixed absolute far_width would need separately rescaling every time either changes. 2.0 matches the common near:far rule of thumb (roughly 1:2). The gap (far_width - wing_width) is the real tail this construction carries until rolled -- see fly.bwb_payoff, fly.position_floor's bwb branch. Placeholder pending recalibration once real sessions exist.
defaults._min_bwb_credit_pct_of_tail: The entry credit is rent for the tail, so it is measured against the tail (far_width - wing_width), not against wing_width the way legged's credit gates are -- there is no width-bounded ceiling here since the structure's own worst case is already wing_width - far_width, not -wing_width.
defaults._max_bwb_credit_pct_of_tail: Ceiling, same intrinsic-heavy-credit logic as legged's own ceiling, measured against the tail instead of wing_width.
defaults._max_bwb_tail_dollars: Hard dollar cap on the tail risk a single bwb may carry (net of its own credit and open fee), independent of how the price-ratio gates above happen to price it. Placeholder pending recalibration.

_arms_note: Each arm differs from control in EXACTLY one thing, each with its own book. control is what makes every other arm falsifiable: gex vs control isolates centring, time_window vs control isolates timing, and the width-N arms vs control sweep wing width in STRIKE increments, not points (control at the default width is the sweep's 1-strike rung — a width-1 arm would duplicate its book under a second name). wide_wing was the single-point version of the width question; it stays for the SPX-era books' attribution but is disabled now the sweep covers it.

control._note: ATM, same window and position cap as the gex arm. The shared baseline for EVERY comparison: gex vs control isolates the CENTRING rule (identical windows), time_window vs control isolates the TIMING (identical centring), width-N vs control isolates the WINGS. It must therefore match gex on everything except where it centres — and it doubles as the width sweep's 1-increment rung, since it trades the default wing_width.
control._history_note: This was a single 12:00-12:15 window with max_positions 2, against gex's 09:45-14:30 and 4 — a 19x difference in entry opportunity. Per-trade metrics survive that, but net P&L per arm does not: the gex arm could have out-earned control purely by trading more often, and the headline comparison would have measured trade count rather than the GEX signal.
control._occupancy_artefact_note: READING CAVEAT 2026-08-04, no code change — see docs/centre-lag.md. An ATM arm plus center_already_occupied is not a neutral baseline on a trending day: control can only open a strike it does not already hold, so the first moment a new ATM strike frees up is the moment spot has just crossed into the LOWER half of that strike's zone. Measured 2026-08-04: all 20 control entries had centre above spot (one-in-a-million under ordinary ATM rounding), which via engine.choose_side put every one of them on the PUT side needing an UP move, on a session that only went up — 19 of 20 completed. The occupancy gate had quietly turned the baseline into a trend-follower. It mirrors on a down day and stalls on a chop day, so do NOT read a control win as evidence that ATM centring beats a signal; check the session's drift and the centre-vs-spot sign first. Compounding this on the same session, $521 of control's $613 came from two flies whose centres happened to sit on the settlement price.

arms._intraday_arms: The intraday agent plan's two arms (packages/flies/docs/intraday-agent-plan.md), added 2026-10-06, each control plus one variable. Add to your own config's arms to run them: "trend-rule": {"enabled": true, "refuse_completion_against_trend": true, "tag_closes": "rule"} -- the trend gate (refuse an entry whose completion needs the day to turn against a committed drift of regime_trend_points) and TAGGED closes of a stranded vertical through its short but not past its wing on a day committed against it, priced at natural and never executed (close_tags.py; run.py close-tags); the arm the agent must beat. "intraday-agent": {"enabled": true, "refuse_completion_against_trend": true, "trend_gate_source": "agent", "tag_closes": "agent"} -- trend-rule's gate switched by the agent's fresh decision (10-minute expiry; trend-rule's gate exactly when there is none) and the closes the agent names, tagged the same way; needs intraday_agent.enabled below and the scripts/flies_intraday_agent.py job.
arms._debit-first-atm: debit-first's ATM twin, added 2026-08-07, for the identical reason as bwb-atm: debit-first overrides entry_modes AND center_rule, a confound this module's own notes already acknowledged carrying ('gives up a clean ATM-vs-ATM control pairing'). debit-first-atm vs control isolates the LEGGING ORDER; debit-first-atm vs debit-first isolates the centring. Fixing one arm's confound and not the other would leave the comparison table inconsistent about what it is measuring.
arms._debit-first-delta-pair: The OTM debit-first pair, added 2026-09-19. THE TRADE: buy a cheap debit vertical whose centre sits at a target delta away from spot (center_rule: delta, debit_delta_target 0.15 -- a magnitude, so it is the 0.15 call going up and the -0.15 put going down), then complete by SELLING the same-centre credit spread once spot has walked into it: at that point the completing spread is near the money and worth several times the debit paid, and the result is a risk-free fly peaked where spot NOW is. The uncompleted branch is bounded at the debit (a few tens of dollars on a 5-wide), never legged's -W tail. This is the trade debit-first was meant to be and never was: the GEX-centred arm always bought the near-ATM spread, because select_center had no rule that placed a centre away from spot. WHY DELTA AND NOT A STRIKE OFFSET: 15 delta is ~40 points out at 10:30 and ~10 at 14:00, so a delta target is one trade all day where spot + N strikes is a different trade every hour; the offset the rule lands on is still recorded per row (center_offset_value), and the delta it chose on is stamped as entry_center_delta, so the 0.15 can be re-cut later rather than needing a second pair per value. TWO ARMS, ONE VARIABLE: up and down differ in direction and nothing else, so the pair's difference IS the direction. Both run every session in paper (capital is unbounded), and 'should direction follow the day' is a re-cut of their rows on the trend_bucket already tagged at entry -- a replay, not a third arm. KEEP THEM IDENTICAL apart from center_direction (a test pins this). min_debit_pct_of_width is overridden to 0.02 here because the shared 0.20 floor (1.00 on a 5-wide) exists to keep the ATM debit arm out of implausibly thin spreads, and a 15-delta spread is that thin by design; debit_cannot_be_out_earned still refuses a spread that cannot pay for itself. debit_delta_tolerance (0.05) is how far from target the nearest strike may sit before the tick is refused rather than centred on the wrong probability -- a refusal, never an ATM degrade, per the call_wall posture. Delta is read off the shared cache's stream_greeks at the QUOTE age limit, not the GEX one; a chain with no fresh delta refuses as no_delta_quotes_beyond_spot. What retires the pair: 15-20 sessions against control on completion rate, net after fees, and the drift-alignment split; if neither direction pays, the bounded strand is being realised too often to matter, which is the finding.
arms._bwb-delta-pairs: The delta-placed bwb pairs, added 2026-09-19: bwb-up/bwb-down at the default width and bwb-up-w2/bwb-down-w2 at wing_width_strikes 2, all on center_rule delta at the SAME 0.15 target as debit-first-up/down. WHY THE SAME RULE: at a centre K and width w a put bwb is +1 (K+w) / -2 K / +1 (K-f), and debit-first-down at the same K buys +1 (K+w) / -1 K and later sells -1 K / +1 (K-w) -- so a bwb IS debit-first with the completion sold at entry for a wider (cheaper) wing, paid for by carrying the tail until the roll buys it back. Placed by the same rule in the same session the two constructions sit on the same strikes and differ in one thing: credit now with a tail, or debit now with none and a conditional completion. WHAT AUGUST DID NOT MEASURE: the bwb arm was never falsified -- 25 rows voided by the roll-pricing defect, the roll unreachable by the legged side rule until 08-07, retired 08-21 with no sample after the fix and its ATM twin never run (see docs/experiment-log.md). THE CREDIT FLOOR IS NOT LOOSENED: min_bwb_credit_pct_of_tail stays at the default, and the 08-07 note is blunt that pushing a bwb out of the money collapses its credit, so these arms are expected to be refused by their own floor much of the time -- the refusal count is a result, not a bug. entry_far_wing_delta is stamped on every row (the chain's own P(tail)) so that flat floor can be re-derived against P(tail) x tail once rows carry it. TWO WIDTHS, DECLARED: practitioners' 0DTE SPX bwbs run 20-50 wide and at 5/10 a 15-delta credit may be near zero, so the w2 pair (10/20) runs beside the default; the tail is far_width - wing_width dollars and scales with it, hence a per-width max_bwb_tail_dollars. Paper only, never a live candidate at that size. Read the roll as the result: best_roll_debit says whether the tail was ever buyable back, and unrolled vs rolled P&L is the answer to the researched trap in docs/faq.md. No hedge overlay here: the tail IS the far wing and insuring it is the roll's job. Direction vs the day is a re-cut on trend_bucket, the same replay as the debit-first pair.
arms._bwb-atm: bwb's ATM twin, added 2026-08-07 -- the CONTROL the bwb arm never had. `bwb` overrides BOTH entry_modes and center_rule, so it differs from `control` in two things at once and cannot attribute a result to either, against this file's own one-variable rule above. This pins centring to ATM so the pair reads three ways: bwb-atm vs control isolates the CONSTRUCTION (bwb_roll vs legged), bwb-atm vs bwb isolates the CENTRING. Note ATM means the structure STRADDLES spot (the near wing lands ~1 strike the other side of it), which is not the fully-OTM placement -- but the roll span (centre +/- wing .. centre +/- far) is still OTM under choose_bwb_side either way, and a straddling structure clears min_bwb_credit_pct_of_tail MORE easily, since a bwb credit is capped by (C(K+w) - C(K+f)) and that gap collapses as the structure is pushed out. Keep max_positions equal to bwb's or the comparison measures opportunity count.
arms._width_arms_note: The width sweep, DISABLED 2026-08-01 with the move to SPX: the arms pinned wing_width to a raw POINT value (2..5), which are not multiples of SPX's 5-point strike spacing and so could not be built there at all. RE-ENABLED 2026-08-15 on a different axis: wing_width_strikes pins the wing to N STRIKE INCREMENTS instead of N points (resolved to points by engine.merged_params against strike_increment), so the sweep means the same thing on any symbol's chain regardless of that symbol's own strike spacing -- 10/15/20/25/50 points on SPX today (control's default wing_width of 5 is the 1-strike rung, which is why there is still no width-1 arm: it would duplicate control's book under a second name). The XSP-era rows under these same arm names used the OLD point-value meaning and are not poolable with the SPX rows that follow; the console's era filter already separates them by symbol.

_advice_note: The loop side of the agentic layer: an out-of-band advisor (packages/advisor) proposes parameter values, and paper_loop.advice_decision re-validates them with cherrypick.core.advice against the 'bounds' manifest below before ANY of them reach a book. OFF by default, and off twice over -- the suite's own advisor.modules.flies switch must also be on. What it does when on: each admitted experiment runs as its own SYNTHETIC ARM, 'advised:<experiment name>' (2026-09-17; one arm per entry in the artifact, each the base arm the entry names plus that entry's params), beside the un-advised base, so the comparison is paired on the same sessions and the same underlying and `control` never changes meaning mid-experiment. An advised arm is a NEW BOOK, not a measurement break in an existing one, and two experiments on control are two twins of the same control rather than one queued behind the other. Absent, stale, expired or invalid advice all mean baseline -- the loop reads once at session start (data/flies/advice_active.json pins the day's decision so it cannot change mid-session) and never waits for, retries, or alerts about advice. There is no management twin because this module has no exits: a book holds to settlement, and settlement covers any advised book that still has rows for the day whatever today's advice says. Only keys listed in 'bounds' can move, only inside their declared closed range, and ONE out-of-range value rejects that experiment's whole overlay (its baseline day; the other entries still open their arms). Entry-side geometry that changes WHICH structures open is a legitimate thing to test, but keep the bounds narrow: an advised book that differs from control on five axes measures nothing.

max_forecast_range_points._note: The containment gate (engine.evaluate_credit_spread_entry): the advised book skips a session whose trailing realized range (provider._trailing_range, prior 5 sessions) exceeds this many points. Declared 2026-09-02 for the advisor's band-containment experiment; the advisor sweeps the cap. Off on every other arm.

miss_stop_minutes._note: engine.miss_stop_refusal (2026-09-17): the advised book stops entering for the day once any of its spreads has sat uncompleted this many minutes. The era's losing sessions were runs of misses into the same tape; this is the live pilot's one-incomplete rule with a clock on it, for an arm with unbounded capital. Replay first: `python -m cherrypick.flies.cli replay-gates`.

refuse_trend_bucket._note: engine.trend_bucket_refusal (2026-09-17): the advised book takes NO entry while the session's trend-from-open bucket (same band as the regime tag) is the named one. Distinct from control-drift's retired side-vs-drift rule: this reads the day, not the leg. Era evidence for control: up_from_open entries completed 66% for -$1,283 across 32; flat/down 77-87% and positive. Too small to act on, the right size to test.

entry_windows._note: The arm's own entry windows as a lever (2026-09-28). Choices: control's own window (the no-op), a late-morning/early-afternoon skip, and 10:30 (the live pilot's start 09-17..09-28). Era evidence for control, net by entry time: 10:00-10:59 +$2,583 on 116 entries, 11:00-12:59 -$580 on 57, 13:00-14:29 +$1,688 on 11 -- but the midday cell is stamped fragile in the regime cuts (dropping one session flips its sign) and open-vs-midday on the same day is 11-7 over 18 sessions, p 0.48. The regime cuts' gate_replay replays every choice here, read off this list. A window only narrows what control would have entered; a choice wider than control's replays as control.
